profile.background: An adult sharing a home with a partner and working at a small community venue. They enjoy setting out the chairs before an event.
profile.history: They have had outpatient treatment for schizophrenia for several years. They recall earlier trouble sleeping and feeling watched. Their days have felt settled for over a year.
profile.organization: Describes events in sequence and can keep different possibilities in mind.
profile.spontaneity: Conversational and comfortable deciding what matters to mention.
profile.guardedness: Open at appointments, selective about who at work knows their health history.
profile.expression: Expressive when discussing music and mildly irritated when plans change at short notice.
profile.self_understanding: Sees sleep, regular treatment, and a reasonably predictable week as parts of staying well.

facts.content: They changed one late shift for an earlier one last week to make time for a concert with their partner.
facts.disclosure_context: A pleasant part of the week.

facts.content: They have not lately felt watched or heard voices.
facts.disclosure_context: Comfortable answering questions about earlier difficulties.

facts.content: They write work shifts and appointments on the same wall calendar.
After a long event they spend ten quiet minutes stacking chairs before heading home.
They take medication in the morning and would like future appointments to fit more easily around work.

dialogue.question: What's been going on in your life since your last visit?
dialogue.answer: Things have felt pretty settled. Last week I swapped one of my late shifts for an earlier shift, which meant my partner and I could go to a concert together. That was a real highlight of the week. I’m still enjoying my work at the venue. I’d like to work out how to fit future appointments around my shifts a bit more easily.

dialogue.question: What would you like us to make time for today?
dialogue.answer: I’d like to work out when I can come to appointments so they fit better with my work shifts. I put both on the same wall calendar. Agreeing on appointment dates ahead of time would help me know how my week will look.

dialogue.question: How has your sleep been over the past week?
dialogue.answer: Do you mean how many hours of sleep I’m actually getting, or whether I’ve had trouble getting to sleep or staying asleep?

dialogue.question: When, if at all, have you felt unsettled recently?
dialogue.answer: I haven’t felt especially unsettled lately. I do find it irritating when a plan changes at the last minute, because I like to have my week laid out. Overall, though, things have felt settled.

dialogue.question: How do you keep track of it all?
dialogue.answer: I keep one wall calendar and put my appointments and my work shifts on it together, so I can see how the week is laid out. It helps to agree on appointment dates ahead of time so I can plan around work.

dialogue.question: I mean dates and times. How do you keep track of work shifts and appointments?
dialogue.answer: I put the dates and times of my shifts on the wall calendar, and do the same for appointments. That lets me see where an appointment fits alongside the shifts.

dialogue.question: What makes that a good sign for you?
dialogue.answer: Do you mean having the week organized? If I have a fairly good idea what the week is going to look like, I find it easier to fit work and treatment together. For me that’s one part of staying well.

dialogue.question: I mean signs that a week is going well. What would count as one for you personally?
dialogue.answer: For me it’s enjoying work and still having time to spend with my partner and enjoy music. The concert we went to last week is a good example. I like having something to look forward to as well as having the week organized.

dialogue.question: Who do you like to spend time with after a busy day?
dialogue.answer: My partner. I like being able to spend time together after I’ve finished work. Going to the concert together last week was a real highlight for me.

dialogue.question: Could you give me a recent example of how you unwound after work?
dialogue.answer: “After a long event at the venue, I take ten quiet minutes to stack the chairs before I head home. I like that part of the routine because it gives me time to unwind before I leave work.”

dialogue.question: How well do the current appointment arrangements fit your life?
dialogue.answer: "They could fit a bit better with my shifts. I’d like to agree on appointment dates ahead of time so I can plan work around them. It’s frustrating when things change at the last minute."

dialogue.question: What else should we cover before you head off?
dialogue.answer: “What I’d mainly like to do before I leave is agree on the next appointment date. That way I can plan around my shifts.”
